# 1 Chronicles Chapter 22 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 381v–382r

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Then David said, "Here shall be the house of the LORD God, and here the altar of burnt offering for Israel."

**2** David commanded that the resident aliens in the land of Israel be gathered, and he set stonecutters to prepare dressed stones for building the house of God.

**3** David provided iron in abundance for nails for the doors of the gates and for clamps, and bronze in abundance beyond weighing,

**4** and cedar logs beyond number, for the Sidonians and Tyrians brought great quantities of cedar to David.

**5** David said, "Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, renowned and glorious throughout all lands. I will therefore make preparation for it." So David provided materials in great quantity before his death.

**6** Then he called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

**7** David said to Solomon, "My son, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.

**8** But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and have waged great wars. You shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth before me.

**9** Behold, a son shall be born to you who shall be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side, for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel in his days.

**10** He shall build a house for my name. He shall be my son, and I will be his father, and I will establish his royal throne over Israel forever.'

**11** "Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he has spoken concerning you.

**12** Only, may the LORD grant you insight and understanding, and give you charge over Israel, that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.

**13** Then you will prosper if you are careful to observe the statutes and the rules that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be dismayed.

**14** With great pains I have provided for the house of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.

**15** You have an abundance of workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and every kind of craftsman skilled in every kind of work.

**16** The gold, silver, bronze, and iron are without limit. Arise and work! The LORD be with you."

**17** David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,

**18** "Is not the LORD your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people.

**19** Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God may be brought into a house built for the name of the LORD."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is unique to Chronicles — it has no parallel in Samuel or Kings. It serves as the bridge between David's acquisition of the temple site (ch.21) and his organization of temple personnel (ch.23-27). The theological centerpiece is v.8: David explains that his disqualification from temple-building is due to bloodshed, not divine rejection. The wordplay between Solomon (*shelomoh*) and peace (*shalom*) in v.9 encodes the son's destiny in his name. David's charge to Solomon (vv.11-13) deliberately echoes Moses' charge to Joshua (Deut 31; Josh 1), establishing a typological parallel: Moses/David prepare, Joshua/Solomon complete. The hyperbolic treasury figures (v.14) express theological rather than economic reality.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "resident aliens" vs. "foreigners"
- **EMET:** "the-sojourners [ha-gerim]"
- **LOGOS:** "the resident aliens"
- **PNEUMA:** "the foreigners living in Israel"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the resident aliens" — *gerim* is a technical term for non-Israelites with protected legal status, not generic "foreigners." LOGOS preserves this distinction.

### V.5 — "young and tender/inexperienced"
- **EMET:** "young [na'ar] and-tender [varakh]"
- **LOGOS:** "young and inexperienced"
- **PNEUMA:** "young and untested"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "young and inexperienced" — the Hebrew *rakh* literally means "tender/soft." LOGOS interprets it as "inexperienced," which captures the contextual sense. PNEUMA's "untested" goes further than the text warrants.

### V.9 — "man of rest" vs. "man of peace"
- **EMET:** "a-man of-rest [ish menuchah]"
- **LOGOS:** "a man of rest"
- **PNEUMA:** "a man of peace"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a man of peace" — while EMET is literally correct (*menuchah* = rest), the context — the wordplay with *shelomoh/shalom*, the contrast with David's wars — makes "peace" the governing concept. The verse itself moves from "rest" to "Solomon" to "peace," and the consensus translation should capture this trajectory.

### V.14 — *be-onyi* — "in my affliction" vs. "with great pains/effort"
- **EMET:** "in-my-affliction [be-onyi]"
- **LOGOS:** "with great effort"
- **PNEUMA:** "I have worked hard"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "with great pains" — a rendering that preserves the ambiguity between suffering/hardship and strenuous effort. The Hebrew *oni* can mean poverty, affliction, or toil.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
